title: Kotlin DSL Shape
intro_html:
How should a Kotlin test author write generated Hamcrest matchers in 6.0.0, and what do we ship for it? Every snippet below is real Kotlin, compiled with Kotlin 2.2.21 against hand-written stand-ins of the generated Java code (JSpecify-annotated, 6.0.0 runtime from the mismatch prototype) and run; the output under each snippet is what the test prints. The failure text is the same for every candidate, because they all end in the same Java matcher: the DSL only changes the call site. Where the candidates really differ is the compile-time checks.

K0 generated Java API as is · K1 docs-only apply { } idiom · K2 the Java generator also emits Consumer lambda overloads (no Kotlin artifact) · K3 separate Kotlin artifact with a per-type wrapper (receiver lambdas, Kotlin names, @DslMarker) · K4 separate generic Kotlin artifact, no per-type code (getter references).
decisions_html:
Q1

Which call-site shape? pick: K2

K2 gives Kotlin the nested-lambda shape (isOrder { it.withId(42L).withCustomer { c -> c.withName("Ada") } }) with no Kotlin code to publish: the Java generator emits one isX(Consumer) per type and one withFoo(Consumer) per property of a generated type. Java users get the same lambdas. Type checks and JSpecify nullness come for free from the Java signatures (N1, N3). Its only cost is the explicit it/c.

K3 reads best (isOrder { id(42L); customer { name("Ada") } }) and is the only shape where @DslMarker stops scope leaks (N2). But it needs per-type Kotlin code: a second, Kotlin-emitting generator (KAPT can write Kotlin sources) in its own artifact. That means a second vocabulary (name() vs withName()), nullability copied into another emitter, and its own docs and tests. That is a lot of permanent surface for a project heading for autopilot.

K4 is rejected on evidence: Java getters need Person::getName because Person::name is still unsupported in Kotlin 2.2 (N4); Person::getAge eq "36" compiles (N3); and its completeness check, which has to rediscover properties at runtime, passes a record with an unchecked component (S10: a false green). K1 adds noise to K0 and lets the outer scope leak silently (N2). K0 stays valid in every option.

Q2

Delivery pick: no Kotlin artifact

With K2 the "Kotlin DSL" is part of the generated Java code of the Hamcrest backend, plus a Kotlin page in the docs backed by a tested Kotlin example module. Production code stays plain Java with no exception. With K3 it would be a separate artifact (e.g. hamcrest-matcher-generator-kotlin) holding a Kotlin-emitting processor, which users add as a second kapt dependency.

Q3

Backend scope pick: Hamcrest only

AssertJ is already fluent from Kotlin (A1, A2): hasCustomerSatisfying { assertThat(it).hasName("Ada") }, and the generated assertThat overloads coexist with AssertJ's own in one import list. K2's Consumer overloads only fill a gap that Hamcrest has. (The OrderLine@2b2948e2 in A2 is the representation topic already settled in Mismatch message format: an opt-in generated Representation.)

Q4

K2 naming pick: overload

withCustomer(Consumer<CustomerMatcher>) is an overload of withCustomer(Customer) and withCustomer(Matcher). That works in Kotlin and in Java (Matcher is not a functional interface). The alternative is a distinct name such as withCustomerMatching { }. Dependencies: JSpecify on the generated code (decided) and the Kotlin getter fix (only matters for Kotlin model classes, unchanged by this choice).
